title: Organelles and their functions
blurb: Match every organelle to its job, trace a secreted protein from ribosome to membrane, and separate the look-alike pairs.
question: A pancreatic cell makes large amounts of a digestive enzyme for export, while a liver cell spends its day breaking down drugs. Which organelles would each cell have in abundance, and what route does the enzyme take to leave the pancreatic cell?

teach.body: Formal definition: organelles are specialized structures within a cell that each carry out a particular function; in eukaryotes most are enclosed by membranes. Plain English: a eukaryotic cell works like a small factory. The nucleus is the head office holding the blueprints (DNA), ribosomes are the assembly line, the ER and Golgi handle finishing and shipping, mitochondria are the power plant, and lysosomes are the recycling crew.

head: Structure
Main job
Memory hook
teach.caption: The nucleus is wrapped in the nuclear envelope, a double membrane with pores. Ribosomes are not membrane-bound; they float free or sit on rough ER.
This pathway is part of the endomembrane system: nuclear envelope, ER, Golgi, lysosomes, vesicles and plasma membrane.
In muscle cells the smooth ER is called the sarcoplasmic reticulum and stores calcium ions.

teach.h: Power plants with their own DNA
teach.body: Mitochondria carry out aerobic cellular respiration to make ATP. They have a double membrane; the inner membrane folds into cristae around a fluid matrix. Chloroplasts (plants and algae) carry out photosynthesis in stacked thylakoids (grana) surrounded by stroma. Both contain their own circular DNA and ribosomes, have double membranes and divide by binary fission. The endosymbiotic theory says both descend from prokaryotes engulfed by an ancestral cell. Your mitochondria came from your mother.

head: Structure
Main job
teach.caption: Intermediate filaments give the cell mechanical strength. Cilia are many and short; a flagellum is single (or few) and long.

teach.body: Aisha, a nursing applicant, predicts organelle numbers from each cell's job. A pancreatic cell exporting enzymes needs lots of rough ER and Golgi apparatus, the secretion route. A liver cell detoxifying drugs needs extensive smooth ER, plus peroxisomes to break down toxins. A heart muscle cell contracting nonstop needs many mitochondria to supply ATP. Rule: the job of the cell predicts which organelles it has most of.

teach.text: Look-alike traps: ribosomes make PROTEINS and smooth ER makes LIPIDS (not the reverse); the Golgi MODIFIES and packages proteins but does not make them; the nucleOLUS makes ribosomal RNA, while the nucleus holds the DNA; lysosomes digest, peroxisomes detoxify with catalase.

items: Nucleus: DNA and control. Nucleolus: rRNA and ribosome subunits.
Ribosomes make protein; rough ER folds it; Golgi modifies, sorts and packages it.
Smooth ER: lipids, steroids, detoxification, calcium storage.
Lysosomes digest with hydrolytic enzymes; peroxisomes use catalase on H₂O₂.
Mitochondria (ATP) and chloroplasts (photosynthesis) have their own DNA: endosymbiosis.
Microtubules build the spindle, cilia and flagella.

summary: You can now match each organelle to its function, trace a secreted protein from rough ER through the Golgi to exocytosis, and predict which organelles a cell has in abundance from the job it does. You can also separate the classic look-alikes: nucleus vs nucleolus, rough vs smooth ER, lysosome vs peroxisome.

A.q: Which organelle modifies, sorts and packages proteins into vesicles for secretion or delivery?
A.why: The Golgi apparatus is the cell's post office: it modifies, sorts and packages proteins and lipids into vesicles.

whyNot.0: Rough ER makes and folds proteins, then sends them on to the Golgi for finishing and packaging.
whyNot.2: Smooth ER makes lipids and steroids and detoxifies; it does not package proteins for export.
whyNot.3: Lysosomes digest materials with hydrolytic enzymes; they are made by the Golgi, not the packager.

A.q: Ribosomes are responsible for which cellular process?
options: Making ribosomal RNA in the nucleus
A.why: Ribosomes carry out protein synthesis (translation), linking amino acids with peptide bonds.

whyNot.1: Lipid and steroid synthesis is the job of the smooth ER.
whyNot.2: Ribosomal RNA is made by the nucleolus, which then assembles ribosome subunits.
whyNot.3: Digesting worn-out organelles is the job of lysosomes.

A.q: Which structure inside the nucleus makes ribosomal RNA and assembles ribosome subunits?
A.why: The nucleolus, inside the nucleus, makes rRNA and assembles the ribosome subunits.

whyNot.0: The nuclear envelope is the double membrane with pores that surrounds the nucleus.
whyNot.1: Chromatin is the DNA-protein material that carries genes; it does not build ribosomes.
whyNot.3: The centrosome lies outside the nucleus and organizes microtubules for the spindle.

B.q: A pancreatic cell secretes a digestive enzyme. Which sequence shows the enzyme's path from synthesis to release?
options: Golgi → vesicle → rough ER → vesicle → membrane
Smooth ER → vesicle → Golgi → lysosome → membrane
Rough ER → vesicle → lysosome → Golgi → membrane
Rough ER → vesicle → Golgi → vesicle → membrane
B.why: Secreted proteins are made on rough ER, carried by a transport vesicle to the Golgi, then shipped in a secretory vesicle to the plasma membrane for exocytosis.

whyNot.0: The Golgi receives proteins from the ER; it does not send them back to the ER for export.
whyNot.1: Smooth ER has no ribosomes, and lysosomes digest material rather than deliver exports.
whyNot.2: Lysosomes are not a stop on the secretion route; the vesicle goes straight to the Golgi.

B.q: Which cell would you expect to contain the greatest number of mitochondria?
B.why: Mitochondria supply ATP, and heart muscle contracts continuously, so its cells are packed with mitochondria.

whyNot.0: Fat cells mainly store lipid and have a low energy demand.
whyNot.1: Surface skin cells have far lower energy needs than constantly contracting muscle.
whyNot.3: Cartilage cells are relatively inactive metabolically, so they need fewer mitochondria.

B.q: Which organelle uses the enzyme catalase to convert hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen?
B.why: Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and toxins, and their catalase converts H₂O₂ into water and O₂.

whyNot.1: Lysosomes hold acidic hydrolytic enzymes for digestion; catalase is the peroxisome's enzyme.
whyNot.2: Smooth ER detoxifies drugs and makes lipids, but catalase is not its signature enzyme.
whyNot.3: The Golgi modifies and packages proteins; it does not break down hydrogen peroxide.

C.q: A patient's liver cells are repeatedly exposed to a drug that must be detoxified. Which organelle would these cells be expected to expand?
C.why: Smooth ER carries out detoxification in liver cells, so repeated drug exposure expands it.

whyNot.0: Rough ER makes and folds proteins; detoxification is a smooth ER job.
whyNot.1: The Golgi packages proteins for export; it does not detoxify drugs.
whyNot.2: Lysosomes digest worn-out organelles and engulfed material, not drugs dissolved in the cell.

C.q: Which statement about mitochondria is CORRECT?
options: They are absent from leaf and root cells
They contain their own circular DNA
They are inherited from the father
They capture light to make glucose
C.why: Mitochondria carry their own circular DNA and ribosomes, evidence for the endosymbiotic theory.

whyNot.0: Plant cells, including leaf and root cells, have mitochondria as well as chloroplasts.
whyNot.2: Mitochondria are inherited from the mother, through the egg.
whyNot.3: Capturing light to make glucose is photosynthesis, which happens in chloroplasts.

C.q: During mitosis in an animal cell, which cytoskeletal structures form the spindle fibers that move the chromosomes?
C.why: Spindle fibers are microtubules (made of tubulin), organized by the centrosome and centrioles.

whyNot.0: Microfilaments (actin) maintain cell shape and pinch the cell in two during cytokinesis.
whyNot.1: Intermediate filaments give mechanical strength; they do not form the spindle.
whyNot.3: Chromatin is the DNA-protein material being moved, not the fibers that move it.

reteach.title: The cell as a factory
reteach.question: Picture a factory that designs, builds and ships a product. Which department matches each organelle?

blocks.body: Head office (nucleus) keeps the master blueprints and sends out copies. The assembly line (ribosomes) builds the product. Finishing (rough ER) folds it into shape. The shipping department (Golgi) labels, sorts and boxes it. Delivery trucks (vesicles) carry it to the loading dock (plasma membrane). The power plant (mitochondria) keeps everything running, and the recycling crew (lysosomes) breaks down broken equipment.

blocks.text: Shipping does not build the product: the Golgi modifies and packages proteins, but ribosomes make them.

explain.body: The nucleus holds the DNA as chromatin and controls the cell; its double-membrane nuclear envelope has pores. The nucleolus, inside the nucleus, makes ribosomal RNA and assembles ribosome subunits.

test.q: Which function belongs to the nucleus as a whole rather than to the nucleolus?
options: Holding the cell's DNA as chromatin
test.why: The nucleus stores the cell's DNA as chromatin and controls cell activity.

whyNot.1: Assembling ribosome subunits is the specific job of the nucleolus.
whyNot.2: Making ribosomal RNA is also the nucleolus's job.
whyNot.3: Packaging proteins into vesicles is done by the Golgi apparatus, outside the nucleus.

explain.body: Ribosomes build proteins. Ribosomes on the rough ER make proteins for secretion, membranes and lysosomes; the rough ER folds them; the Golgi modifies, sorts and packages them into vesicles.

test.q: Which organelle is studded with ribosomes and folds proteins destined for secretion?
test.why: Rough ER is covered in ribosomes, giving it a rough look, and folds the proteins they make.

whyNot.0: Smooth ER has no ribosomes; it makes lipids and steroids.
whyNot.2: The Golgi receives proteins from the rough ER and packages them; it has no ribosomes.
whyNot.3: The nucleolus builds ribosome subunits but does not fold secreted proteins.

explain.body: Smooth ER makes lipids and steroids, detoxifies (especially in liver) and stores calcium. Lysosomes use acidic hydrolytic enzymes to digest worn-out organelles, food particles and engulfed bacteria. Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and toxins; catalase turns H₂O₂ into water and O₂.

test.q: A neutrophil engulfs a bacterium. Which organelle supplies the hydrolytic enzymes that digest it?
test.why: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes in an acidic interior and digest engulfed bacteria.

whyNot.0: Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and hydrogen peroxide, not engulfed bacteria.
whyNot.1: The Golgi makes lysosomes but does not itself digest engulfed material.
whyNot.2: Smooth ER detoxifies dissolved chemicals; it does not digest whole bacteria.

explain.body: Mitochondria make ATP by aerobic respiration (cristae, matrix). Chloroplasts do photosynthesis. Both have double membranes, their own DNA and ribosomes, and divide by binary fission: the evidence for endosymbiotic theory. The cytoskeleton (microtubules, microfilaments, intermediate filaments) gives shape and movement.

test.q: Which feature of mitochondria supports the endosymbiotic theory?
options: Own circular DNA and a double membrane
A single outer membrane, like lysosomes
Division by mitosis with the nucleus
test.why: Their own circular DNA, double membrane and division by binary fission all resemble an engulfed prokaryote.

whyNot.1: Mitochondria have a double membrane, not a single one.
whyNot.2: The Golgi makes lysosomes and vesicles, not mitochondria.
whyNot.3: Mitochondria divide by binary fission, separately from mitosis of the nucleus.
